  "candidate_rtl": "module mul_subexpression(\n    input [7:0] multiplicand,\n    input [7:0] multiplier,\n    output [15:0] product\n);\nassign product = multiplicand * multiplier;\nendmodule",
  "bottleneck": "The original RTL creates eight partial-product rows and then accumulates them using a serial chain of seven 16-bit carry-propagate additions. This explicit dependency chain is likely to result in a longer critical path if the synthesizer preserves the accumulation order, rather than allowing a parallel carry-save or compressor tree.",
  "rewrite": "Replace the explicit partial-product rows and serial adder accumulation with a single unsigned multiplication operator. This removes the source-level serial dependency and lets Yosys/ABC infer an optimized parallel multiplier structure, such as carry-save compression or Booth recoding, with shallower logic depth.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "Estimated 10-30% reduction in maximum data arrival, roughly 0.3-0.8 ns improvement over the 2.78 ns baseline under the same conditions. This is a hypothesis to be verified by EDA.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "Expected area similar to or lower than baseline because the explicit partial-product row wires and seven 16-bit adder trees are removed. Even if a parallel multiplier uses slightly more cells, the area cap provides about 296.5 um^2 (10%) headroom above the 2965.344 um^2 baseline, so compliance is likely.",
  "functional_boundaries": "Preserves exact module name, input/output ports, 8-bit unsigned inputs, 16-bit unsigned full product, and all 2^16 input combinations. No clocks, state elements, don't-cares, or input restrictions are introduced."
}
